blocks.text: Posted in 'Local Work': Got the Flour & Salt delivery trike back on the road yesterday. Their whole three-speed was rusted solid—chain, hub, the works. Cleaned and lubed everything I could salvage, replaced the chain and one cog. They didn’t miss a single morning drop-off. Good as new.

Good to hear, Ember. Speaking of your shop—those ventilation fans are in. Your lintels aren't standard, so I had to bend the bracket arms to fit. They’re secure now. You’ll want to run them for an hour before any heavy sanding to clear the air.
Thanks, Mabel. That’s a huge help. We tested them this morning and the draft is strong. No more sawdust fog.

Efficient work, both of you. Meanwhile, I sat on my hands for two days on a South Copse job waiting for a city inspector to come stamp the breaker box. Client’s shop renovation just… paused. Everything was up to code and ready Monday morning. He showed up Wednesday afternoon.
That’s the worst. You call the scheduler every day?
Twice a day. They just say he’s behind. Nothing to do but wait and eat the delay.
Ember, that was our trike. Thank you. We didn’t realize how bad it was until it just stopped. You saved our week.
Glad it worked out. Keep an eye on the chain tension; it might stretch a bit over the next week.
At least someone’s machinery is moving. My inspector finally came, stamped it, took thirty seconds. Job’s done now. But two days.
We need a better system for that. Maybe the Chamber circle can poke the Wizard’s Office about inspection delays. It’s not just you.
